Ballymun-Finglas (Ballymun, Finglas, Santry) — Dublin, Ireland

In detail

This LEA — covering Ballymun, Finglas, and Santry — shows a well-documented, ongoing pattern of gangland violence concentrated in Ballymun and Finglas, with Santry itself returning no notable safety coverage. Finglas has a long-running drugs-related feud: in November 2023, 23-year-old Brandon Ledwidge was shot dead in a gangland attack tied to a drugs gang dispute, with houses subsequently boarded up as the feud escalated (Irish Times). Fatal stabbings followed in June 2024 and again in November 2024, when a man in his 60s (Mark Carroll) died after an assault, though gardai said he was not the intended target (RTE, Irish Times, Irish Examiner). Ballymun has seen an intensifying and very current feud: a house was petrol-bombed with two people hospitalised, a house was left with bullet holes after a shooting, and a bullet was fired into the bedroom of a sleeping three-year-old, alongside a grenade-style explosion that damaged four homes in May 2026 (Crime World, TheJournal.ie). In October 2025 a man in his 30s was seriously injured in a broad-daylight attack in Ballymun (TheJournal.ie). Most alarmingly, in April 2026 a child discharged a handgun dropped by a suspect fleeing gardai in Ballymun, prompting local representatives to call it a "crisis" requiring government intervention (RTE, Irish Times, dublinpeople.com, Social Democrats statement). Gardai have responded with repeated raids, drug/weapon seizures, and newly launched high-visibility patrols to disrupt criminal activity. Given the frequency, recency, and severity — multiple shootings, murders, explosives, and firearms reaching a child — this pattern is serious and ongoing rather than isolated, though the violence is largely feud-targeted rather than random street crime affecting casual visitors, and daytime incidents are less frequent than nighttime ones. Sources checked: Irish Times (irishtimes.com); RTE (rte.ie); TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); Irish Examiner (irishexaminer.com); Crime World (crimeworld.com); Garda.ie official press releases (garda.ie); Dublin People (dublinpeople.com).
